detail: One token defined once for both themes. Light was 5.5:1, dark 2.9:1. Fixed with a same-hue dark-mode override at 6.16:1 (cell PR #1, commit 4033dae). The template carries the identical bug (#2d6ea8 = 2.96:1 dark) and every stamped cell inherits it until watermill-cell-template issue #2 is fixed. Nothing in make verify checks contrast, so this is a gate hole: the rule is stated in prose only.
text: The stamped default --brand-primary is 2.9:1 against the dark-mode surface, below the 4.5:1 the file header and CLAUDE.md require in both themes.

text: A brand accent sampled from a logo (gold #e8c549, 1.68:1 on white) is a fill or border colour, never light-mode text.

detail: Sluice caught it in cell PR #2 (commit 7e8aa9d). Check any prose fence list entry-for-entry against watermill.yaml fence.paths; the contract is the truth and the doc must say which files are fenced and why the others deliberately are not.
text: A doc that misdescribes the fence can disable a repo rule: CLAUDE.md claimed README.md was fenced, which would forbid the docs-in-the-same-change rule stated one bullet above it.

author: human
detail: Fixed in cell PR #3 (commit d484ad3): reject a body that is not an object or whose username/password is not a string with 400 before SQLite or werkzeug see it; 401 stays for wrong credentials in a well-formed body. Millstone's suite tested only well-formed bodies. Any endpoint reachable without a session must be probed with non-object JSON.
text: request.get_json(silent=True) or {} keeps a JSON array, string or number, so payload.get raised and a non-string username reached SQLite: six of ten malformed login bodies returned 500 with a traceback, unauthenticated.

text: Flask sets HttpOnly but never SameSite on the session cookie; with no CSRF token, set SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE='Lax' explicitly or another origin can POST to logout with the user's cookie.

detail: Mutation test that found it: make seed_demo_users() UPDATE password_hash unconditionally; the suite passed. Added test_seed_does_not_reset_a_changed_password (cell PR #3). The general rule: for 'idempotent' or 'does not touch X', change X between two calls and assert it survived.
text: An idempotence test must assert the state that must not change: test_seed_is_idempotent stayed green when seeding was made to overwrite every password on start.

text: A fetch wrapper's documented promise (credentials: 'same-origin') had no test: deleting the line left the frontend suite green because it is also the browser default.

detail: Millstone had a reset branch inside the effect and removed it because react-hooks/set-state-in-effect rejected it, leaving the leak. The shape that satisfies the lint rule: tag fetched state with the session it belongs to and compare during render, not in an effect. Fixed in cell PR #4 (e16a9f9) with two tests that drive a real logout/login through the DOM, one holding the second fetch open to assert on exactly the stale window. The cancellation flag was correct; the bug was the stale render, not a stale write.
text: Per-session React state (modules list, fetch error) was never reset on user change, so logging out and in as another role rendered the previous role's cards, and one failed fetch stuck its error on screen for every later session until reload.

author: human
detail: Fixed in cell PR #4: /api paths return a JSON 404 before the SPA fallback; /, client-side routes and /assets/* still serve. The template's app.py has the same fallback shape. Any test for an unknown API id must assert the status code, not just that the call did not throw.
text: The SPA catch-all served index.html with 200 for unknown /api/* paths, so GET /api/modules/nope was a 200 whose body the client turned into {} and docs/dashboard.md in the same PR called it a 404.

detail: PRs #1-#4 on zim-dashboard-demo-cell-1b, 2026-08-30. Review-found defects: dark-mode contrast; 500 on malformed login JSON, missing SameSite, two tests that passed broken code; cross-session state leak, SPA fallback swallowing API 404s, 500 on role-less session, stubs with no caller. A green millstone gate is necessary, not sufficient; sluice's independent mutation testing is where the value was.
text: Standing up the cell skeleton took 4 PRs and every one was approve_after_fixes: sluice found real bugs in all three code PRs and a contract contradiction in the docs PR; millstone's own suites passed every one of them.

text: The auto-mode Bash classifier can block a plain 'gh pr merge' once as a false positive; re-running the identical command alone succeeds, so retry before reporting a merge failure.

author: human
detail: Parking is a write. Fixed in cell PR #7 (f3e8a6f): dry-run counts the failure in RunResult.exceptions and the pipeline_runs row without parking. Rule for any dry-run flag: enumerate every table the code path touches and assert row counts are unchanged after a dry run, not just the primary sink.
text: dry_run=True still wrote to review_queue: four --dry-run invocations left four identical pending rows in a human's work queue while the docs sold dry-run as side-effect free.

detail: Same class as zimmy-life-tracker bead 0p5 (one unresolvable job registers none). Fixed in cell PR #7: each registration is guarded and a failure costs only itself. Test: a schedule naming a missing pipeline still starts the others.
text: scheduler.start() did a bare PIPELINES[name]() per schedule entry, so one schedule with no implementation raised KeyError out of start() and, since app.py calls start() before run(), no app at all.

author: human
text: A fixture whose only bad record is last cannot test 'one bad record must not abort the batch': continue → break passed every test until the bad record was moved to the middle.

author: human
text: When a pre-check shadows a defence-in-depth layer (run()'s has() before RecordingAdapter.write()'s own refusal), the inner layer has zero coverage: deleting it changed nothing. Test each layer by bypassing the one above it.

author: human
text: RecordingAdapter idempotency is per-process, so the cloud-cron entry 'python -m services.pipelines <name>' run twice wrote twice; a demo that must prove cross-run dedup needs a persisted key set.

author: human
detail: Set before BEGIN, sqlite3 runs the pragma in autocommit and it is cleared before the first DELETE — sluice's first fix attempt failed exactly that way (cell PR #11, b4d8530). Later generalised to the whole load in PR #14 because fixtures load alphabetically (grants.json before organisations.json). The negative test must distinguish deferred from disabled: mutating to PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF kept the suite green until a dangling-org_id-fails-at-COMMIT test was added (PR #14, 9ae4fd0).
text: python -m services.seed --reset died with a raw FOREIGN KEY IntegrityError once users.org_id referenced a fixture-owned table — DELETE-then-reload needs PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys ON set INSIDE the explicit BEGIN, not before it.

author: human
detail: seed_demo_users() continue'd past existing rows, so only fresh DBs got org_id. Fix (PR #11): backfill when the column is NULL ('never assigned'), never overwrite non-NULL (a decision), never rewrite password_hash/role. General rule: when a migration adds a column the seeder owns, the seeder must define upgrade semantics, not just insert semantics.
text: A migration that adds a column NULL plus an insert-only seeder left the pre-existing demo Client org-less forever — /api/organisations/me 404'd for the primary demo login on every upgraded DB.

author: human
detail: Also: 'Infinity' escaped as OverflowError instead of the documented ValueError. And the Decimal-vs-float mutation test needed an adversarial value — '12.34' and '-0.05' round-trip fine under float; '19.99' drifts (1998.999→1998). Cell PR #13, d1fb2e5.
text: Sub-cent money amounts were silently banker's-rounded: Decimal to_integral_value() turned '0.005' into 0 cents and '0.015' into 2 — undocumented ROUND_HALF_EVEN on money; now a ValueError.

author: human
detail: Suite must run under multiple TZs to see it (sluice reran under TZ=UTC, America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo — cell PR #13). Same family as the repo's clock.today() rule; epoch conversions of naive datetimes are where it leaks back in.
text: A naive datetime passed as 'since' was read as LOCAL time by .timestamp() — a 4-hour filter shift on US/Eastern that a UTC CI runner can never catch; naive now means UTC.

detail: Workaround: non-seed JSON lives in a subdirectory (data-fixtures/finance/, data-fixtures/grants/) — _fixture_paths is a non-recursive listdir. Undiscoverable from the failure it causes; bead e7m.11 (P2) makes the loader skip or label non-fixture files.
text: services/seed.py scanned every top-level data-fixtures/*.json as a {table,key,rows} fixture, so one non-fixture JSON (a SimpleFIN feed) crash-looped create_app() and broke 76 of 135 tests.

author: human
detail: When two parallel beads may need the same infrastructure, name the shared artifact (exact table name and CREATE text) in BOTH briefs up front, or serialise the bead that creates it. The union-merge append-at-end convention for db.py SCHEMA/MIGRATIONS and docs tables worked; the rebase (PR #14 onto #13's main) was clean because the semantic switch had already been done as a fix-up commit.
text: Two parallel millstones invented two tables for the same job (recorded_writes vs monday_recorded_writes) because the generic-table guidance reached only one brief; the orchestrator had to arbitrate and one PR rebased to adopt the other's table.

author: human
detail: Fix (cell PR #15, 8526302): the INSERT catches sqlite3.IntegrityError from the partial-unique race, rolls back, falls through to the update path, re-raises anything else. Rule: any 'safe under concurrency' claim must name the mechanism; accidental safety from implicit transactions is a regression waiting for a WAL switch.
text: park() was called inside run()'s except handler with no inner try, so a park() exception aborted the entire pipeline run; the observed no-double-row behaviour under races rested on sqlite3's implicit-BEGIN RESERVED lock, not on code.

author: human
text: A dedup migration over live data must pin WHICH row survives: the oldest-pending-row choice was only real once MIN(id)->MAX(id) failed a test; times_seen resets and last_seen_at backfills also needed asserting, not just documenting.
